title: TerraView: Interactive IaC Blueprint Visualizer & Policy Linter
tagline: Parses Terraform configurations, renders active dependency tree diagrams, and runs OPA compliance scans against custom policies.

problemStatement.overview: Reviewing raw Terraform files is error-prone. TerraView compiles code to structured JSON, checks policies against Open Policy Agent guidelines, and presents visual layouts of cloud resource maps.
problemStatement.targetAudience: Cloud Architects, DevOps Engineers, Security compliance officers
userPersonas: Cloud Engineer validating architecture changes before merge requests.
Compliance officer enforcing encrypted disk standard protocols.

systemArchitecture.narrative: A web client tool. Files are parsed using a WebAssembly-compiled version of the HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language) parser. Diagrams are drawn dynamically, and OPA rules are applied locally.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: Upload HCL files -> HCL Parser (Wasm) -> AST JSON Node tree -> D3.js visual renderer -> Open Policy Agent validator -> Violations list.

core: Interactive SVG dependency layout tree canvas.
advanced: Cost estimations calculator (integration with Infracost API).
Automatic pull request markdown comment builder.

directoryStructure:
terraview/
├── cli/                 # Rust CLI client
├── wasm-parser/         # HCL parser module compiled to web assembly
├── web/                 # React UI visual graph portal
└── package.json

roadmap.title: HCL parsing to JSON
tasks: Create Rust crate that parses terraform files.
Compile binary dependencies into WebAssembly modules.

deploymentCiCd.containerization: No server needed (purely client-side static files).
steps: Publish builds to Cloudflare edge CDN.

resumeBullets: Developed an interactive Infrastructure-as-Code linter and visualizer utilizing React, Rust, and WebAssembly, rendering SVG node maps of resource trees.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did you compile the parser to WebAssembly rather than running it on a backend?
interviewQuestions.answerHint: Highlight the benefits of client-side computation (zero hosting cost, immediate feedback, and absolute privacy for sensitive infrastructure files).

title: GlowTracer: Dynamic Distributed Tracing and Profiling CLI
tagline: A lightweight CLI tool monitoring latency in localized systems, compiling visual flamegraphs in terminal windows.

problemStatement.overview: Legacy profiling tools inject severe runtime latency overheads. GlowTracer uses kernel ebpf hooks to monitor thread run durations non-invasively.
problemStatement.targetAudience: Performance Engineers, Systems Architects, SRE engineers
userPersonas: Kernel performance engineer tracking latency spikes

systemArchitecture.narrative: Hooks run inside kernel ring buffers. CLI reads stack frames and formats active flamegraphs dynamically inside terminal logs.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: eBPF Probe -> Ring Buffer -> Go Parser Daemon -> Frame Compiler -> Console flamegraph.

resumeBullets: Developed distributed profiler utilizing Go, Rust, and eBPF kernel event probes.

title: ConfigGuard: Automated Schema Linter for YAML configuration files
tagline: Statically analyzes helm files and compose configurations, suggesting fixes for security misconfigs.

problemStatement.overview: Misconfigured YAML coordinates lead to container crashes. ConfigGuard runs checks on schemas to identify invalid properties before push commands.

systemArchitecture.narrative: Reads files. Traverses YAML node paths. Emits warnings detailing exact invalid paths and standard values templates.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: YAML File -> Parse Tree -> Rule engine checker -> Validation result map -> Terminal print.

resumeBullets: Created ConfigGuard linting CLI checking yaml files against structural schemas.

title: DockVisual: Local Docker Desktop Container map dashboard
tagline: Renders interactive graph visual networks of running docker setups, volumes, and networks.

problemStatement.overview: Managing multi-container docker compose setups is difficult without a graph mapping of dynamic socket links.
problemStatement.targetAudience: Web Developers, backend engineers, local systems QA
userPersonas: Fullstack dev auditing compose volume mounts

systemArchitecture.narrative: React dashboard communicates via local Docker Socket API. Gathers stats on CPU, network connections, and volume maps.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: Docker socket stream -> Backend parser daemon -> Web sockets -> React UI canvas.

resumeBullets: Engineered DockVisual local diagnostic panel mapping volume attachments and socket links in D3.

title: MockAPI: Zero-Config Local REST server compiler CLI
tagline: Reads schema files and spins up fully compliant mocked servers with custom endpoints and delays.

problemStatement.overview: Frontend developers wait for backend APIs to complete. MockAPI builds routes with realistic mocks and delays in seconds.
problemStatement.targetAudience: Frontend developers, mobile engineers, QA automation crews
userPersonas: Frontend developer coding client screens offline

systemArchitecture.narrative: Reads endpoint definitions in JSON format. Compiles dynamic express routing hooks on target port, generating mocked properties.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: API JSON specification -> MockAPI Engine -> Express Server creation -> Dynamic mock response endpoints.

resumeBullets: Developed MockAPI CLI generating express servers with relational mock database properties.

title: BugSpy: Dynamic Debugger and Console Event Interceptor
tagline: Statically injects logging wrappers into source files, providing call traces without modifying execution code.

problemStatement.overview: Manual console.log insertion is tedious. BugSpy parses abstract syntax trees, automatically wrapping function blocks in telemetry triggers.
problemStatement.targetAudience: Node.js developers, QA automation leads, debuggers
userPersonas: Backend developer tracking recursive function failures

systemArchitecture.narrative: Parses source files into AST. Injects instrumentation logging tokens. Emits traces to Electron visualization dashboard.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: Source code upload -> Babel AST parser -> Instrumentation injection -> Executed code -> BugSpy Trace Dashboard.

resumeBullets: Built BugSpy debugger AST instrumentation tools mapping runtime callback cascades.

title: WasmPacker: High-Performance WebAssembly module bundle builder
tagline: Compiles Rust crates and C headers to optimized WebAssembly targets, generating Typescript bindings.

problemStatement.overview: Wasm build setups are complex. WasmPacker wraps compilation tools, generating typed TypeScript declarations automatically.
problemStatement.targetAudience: Performance Web Developers, audio/video browser engineers, game developers
userPersonas: Web developer compiling video codec processing library

systemArchitecture.narrative: CLI triggers compilation using system rustc/clang compilers. Formats memory layout headers and compiles modern bindings.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: Source files -> WasmPacker -> compiler wrapper -> optimized Wasm binary -> typed TypeScript bridge interface.

resumeBullets: Designed WasmPacker Rust compiler tooling generating TS declarations for Wasm modules.

title: BenchMark: Cloud API Stress and Load Testing Simulator
tagline: Runs distributed load tests from local network endpoints, auditing API performance metrics.

problemStatement.overview: Simulating high concurrency API usage requires complex cloud setups. BenchMark spawns local worker pools executing HTTP requests.
problemStatement.targetAudience: Backend developers, QA automation leads, SRE teams

systemArchitecture.narrative: Multi-threaded worker pool written in Go. WebSockets pipe latency data to visual dashboards using Plotly graphics.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: Configure endpoint -> Spawn Go request worker pool -> WS stream stats -> Plotly dashboard canvas.

resumeBullets: Created BenchMark load tester generating 50k+ concurrent requests securely in Go.

title: SchemaDiff: Database Migration schema auditor
tagline: Scans SQL schema structures, generating incremental safe SQL migration scripts.

problemStatement.overview: Manual SQL migrations lead to data loss. SchemaDiff tracks schema alterations and auto-compiles migration paths.
problemStatement.targetAudience: Database Administrators, backend developers, release teams
userPersonas: Backend dev changing relational model properties

systemArchitecture.narrative: Compares active target database structure with model source definitions. Compiles migration steps securely.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: Model file definitions -> SchemaDiff comparison -> SQL schema comparison -> Migration file generation.

resumeBullets: Developed SchemaDiff migration compiler detecting structural schema changes in Python.

title: GitFlow: Visual Git Branching and Interactive Conflict Resolver
tagline: Renders interactive local git branching structures and provides merge conflict GUI selectors.

problemStatement.overview: Resolving git conflicts in terminal is complex. GitFlow maps branches visually, highlighting identical conflict lines.
problemStatement.targetAudience: Software engineering teams, students, git users
userPersonas: SDE resolving main merge branches conflicts

systemArchitecture.narrative: React app reads Git CLI inputs. Renders Cytoscape.js graph layout. Highlights conflict tags with choices GUI.
systemArchitecture.dataFlow: Git project files -> Git CLI indexer -> Branch map (Cytoscape) -> React merge choices selector.

resumeBullets: Built GitFlow branch visualizer and conflict resolver GUI utilizing React and Cytoscape.js.
